domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories. The feature scope targets annual, sick, and emergency; unpaid, maternity, and paternity are defined for completeness.

domain_entities.name: LeaveStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Lifecycle states for a LeaveRequest. Governs which transitions and operations are valid at each stage.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT: employee is composing; not visible to manager; editable by employee; can transition to SUBMITTED or CANCELLED
SUBMITTED: awaiting manager decision; not editable; can transition to APPROVED, REJECTED, or CANCELLED
APPROVED: manager granted the leave; immutable except for cancellation; balance has been deducted; can transition to CANCELLED
REJECTED: manager denied the leave; terminal state; no balance impact
CANCELLED: employee withdrew the request; terminal state; if previously APPROVED, balance is restored

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's application for leave. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through terminal states, including who acted and when at each transition.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT → SUBMITTED: employee submits the request; validates policy rules (notice days, balance sufficiency)
DRAFT → CANCELLED: employee discards the draft
SUBMITTED → APPROVED: manager approves; balance is deducted; approvedBy and approvedAt are set
SUBMITTED → REJECTED: manager rejects; rejectedBy and rejectedAt are set; no balance impact
SUBMITTED → CANCELLED: employee withdraws before decision; no balance impact
APPROVED → CANCELLED: employee cancels an approved leave; balance is restored; cancelledBy and cancelledAt are set

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules governing a specific leave type: how many days are entitled, notice requirements, whether manager approval is needed, and accrual caps. One policy per leave type per organizational scope.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE (isActive=true): policy is in effect; governs new leave requests
INACTIVE (isActive=false): policy is retired; does not apply to new requests but historical references remain valid

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, consumption, and remaining balance for a specific leave policy within a fiscal year. One balance record per employee-policy-fiscalYear combination.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE: fiscal year is current; balance is tracked and can be consumed by approved leave requests
EXHAUSTED: remainingDays = 0 while fiscal year is still current; no further leave of this type can be approved unless entitlement is adjusted
CLOSED: fiscal year has ended; balance is read-only and preserved for audit/history

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organization. In the leave domain, employees are requesters (applicants) and managers are approvers. The managerId self-referential relationship establishes the approval hierarchy.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE: employee can apply for leave and (if they have direct reports) approve/reject leave
INACTIVE: employee cannot apply for leave; existing approved leave remains valid
TERMINATED: employee is separated; all pending leave requests are implicitly void; historical records preserved

business_rules: Day counting is inclusive: the number of leave days consumed by a request spanning startDate to endDate is (endDate − startDate + 1) calendar days. This count is used for balance deduction, balance restoration, policy sufficiency checks, and all reporting. Weekends and public holidays are NOT excluded unless a future working-days-only policy is introduced. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance appears, not only here]
A leave request can only be submitted if the employee's employmentStatus is ACTIVE. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, Employee appears, not only here]

On submission, the system validates that the number of calendar days between the submission date and startDate meets or exceeds the LeavePolicy.minimumNoticeDays. If minimumNoticeDays is 0, no notice is required. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeavePolicy appears, not only here]

On submission, the system checks that the employee's LeaveBalance for the matching policy and fiscal year has remainingDays >= the requested number of calendar days (inclusive count). If no balance record exists for that fiscal year, the request is rejected. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

When a leave request transitions to APPROVED, the employee's LeaveBalance.usedDays is incremented by the number of calendar days consumed, and remainingDays is decremented by the same amount. This deduction is atomic with the status transition. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

When an APPROVED leave request is CANCELLED, the balance is restored: LeaveBalance.usedDays is decremented and remainingDays is incremented by the same number of calendar days originally deducted. This restoration is atomic with the status transition. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

Only the employee's designated manager (Employee.managerId) may approve or reject a SUBMITTED leave request. If managerId is null, the request escalates — the system rejects submission with an error indicating no manager is assigned. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, Employee appears, not only here]

A manager cannot approve or reject their own leave request. The approver's employeeId must differ from the request's employeeId. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

LeavePolicy.requiresManagerApproval determines whether the SUBMITTED → APPROVED path requires explicit manager action. When requiresManagerApproval is false, the request auto-approves on submission (skipping SUBMITTED state entirely: DRAFT → APPROVED). When true, the standard manager approval flow applies. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeavePolicy appears, not only here]
endDate must be on or after startDate. A request where endDate < startDate is invalid at submission time. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

The fiscal year for balance lookup is derived from the leave request's startDate. The fiscal year is defined as the calendar year of startDate (January 1 – December 31). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
## Lifecycle states introduced

- **LeaveStatus**: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED — governs the LeaveRequest state machine with six named transitions.
- **LeaveBalance status**: ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, CLOSED — tracks fiscal-year lifecycle of a balance record.
- **LeavePolicy isActive**: ACTIVE (true) / INACTIVE (false) — governs whether a policy applies to new requests.
- **Employee employmentStatus**: ACTIVE, INACTIVE, TERMINATED — determines eligibility to apply for leave.

## Key domain decisions

1. **Day counting is inclusive and calendar-based**: (endDate − startDate + 1). This is a broad rule applied uniformly to balance deduction, restoration, sufficiency checks, and reporting. No exclusion of weekends or holidays.

2. **Fiscal year = calendar year of startDate**: Balance lookup uses the year component of the request's startDate. Cross-year requests deduct from a single year.

3. **Manager approval chain**: Only the employee's direct manager (Employee.managerId) can approve/reject. Self-approval is forbidden. When requiresManagerApproval is false, the request auto-approves (DRAFT → APPROVED, skipping SUBMITTED).

4. **Balance deduction/restoration is atomic with status transitions**: APPROVED deducts; CANCELLED (from APPROVED) restores. REJECTED and CANCELLED (from SUBMITTED) have no balance impact.

5. **Three open questions** remain: fiscal year configurability, overlap detection policy, and cross-year balance splitting — these need stakeholder input before the application architect finalizes service logic.

open_questions.question: Should the fiscal year be calendar year (Jan 1 – Dec 31) or a configurable period (e.g., Apr 1 – Mar 31)? The current domain rule uses calendar year of startDate.
open_questions.impact: Affects which LeaveBalance record is used for deduction and how year-end rollover works. If fiscal year is configurable, the LeaveBalance lookup and the CLOSED→ACTIVE transition logic must be parameterized.
candidate_options: Configurable per organization — stored as a setting, more complex but flexible

open_questions.question: Should overlapping leave requests be prevented? E.g., an employee with an existing APPROVED or SUBMITTED request for Jan 5–10 should not be allowed to submit another for Jan 8–12.
open_questions.impact: Without overlap detection, an employee could double-book leave and potentially exceed balance if both are approved before balance is checked. With overlap detection, the submission validation becomes more complex and must consider date-range intersection logic.
candidate_options: No overlap detection — balance check alone is sufficient guard
Prevent overlapping SUBMITTED or APPROVED requests — reject submission if date ranges intersect
Prevent overlapping APPROVED requests only — allow multiple SUBMITTED but reject if any overlap with APPROVED

open_questions.question: When a leave request spans two fiscal years (e.g., Dec 28 – Jan 3), should the balance be deducted from a single fiscal year (the year of startDate) or split across both years?
open_questions.impact: Affects balance deduction logic, balance sufficiency checks, and year-end processing. A split approach requires two balance records and partial deductions; a single-year approach is simpler but may allow gaming across year boundaries.
candidate_options: Single fiscal year (year of startDate) — simpler, current domain rule
Split across fiscal years — days in each calendar year deducted from respective balance records
